Spirit, the granaries are heavy with the last harvest, and my people sleep with full bellies. We have wheat to spare, yes. But I have not seen the smoke of Wewush, nor heard their voices. Where do they lie? Are they men like us, or something else? If they are truly hungry and not wolves in disguise, we will share. But first, tell me where they dwell, so my runners do not walk into the sea.

I hear you, spirit, though dreams are often like mist—they show shapes that are not always there. My people are joyful and our bellies are full; the xi wheat piles high in the granary, more than we can eat before the next snow. It is a good thing to share when the sun shines on us. But who are these Wewush? I have not seen their fires or walked their paths. If they are truly neighbours, tell me where they lie, so my men can find them and carry the grain without getting lost in the deep woods.

Spirit, you speak of a village named Wewush, yet my eyes have never seen their smoke nor my ears heard their drums. We have much wheat in the granary, it is true, more than enough for our bellies. But my people are wary of those we do not know. To send grain to shadows is not wise. If these neighbours are real, tell me truly where they lie, so we do not waste our harvest on ghosts.

You speak of Joawethom, spirit, but my people know this name not. We have walked the coast and the forest for many years, and we have seen no other fires, no other huts. My granaries are full, yes, and the bellies of Wewush are full, but I do not send grain into the mist for a ghost story.

If these neighbors are real, tell me where they lie. If they are close, we would have found them by now. If they are far, how do I reach them? Speak plain, spirit. Where is this Joawethom?
